asserts: A reader that implements feature bit 32 refuses each of these metadata blocks with the rejection class the case names, taking the block's checks in the order spec/v1 fixes, and refuses the block and not the file: where the case's outcome is block-refused, the file opens and is served with no description and no provenance.
contract: Two readers that implement the bit must give one broken block one class, and neither may lose a file's samples to its metadata.
notes: These bind readers that implement bit 32. A reader that does not implement it ignores the bit, the pointer and the block, and opens every block-refused file here. Each file is built with its defect; the cross-order cases patch one field of such a file, outside every block's CRC.

cases.name: v1-metadata-pointer-zero
cases.reason: bit 32 set and the pointer bytes zero: an empty extent at offset 0. This is the header a writer that sets the bit without implementing it writes, and it is the shape of the may-ignore case in v1-negative-vectors, which a reader that implements the bit opens and refuses the block of (v1-metadata-may-ignore-case-under-bit-32, below)

cases.name: v1-metadata-offset-past-eof
cases.reason: the offset lies past the end of the file. The block is refused for that rule, never for whatever a reader's language does when it slices past a buffer

cases.name: v1-metadata-length-past-eof
cases.reason: the offset is the block's own and the length runs past the end of the file

cases.name: v1-metadata-extent-wraps
cases.reason: offset 2^64 - 8 and length 16, whose sum wraps to 8 in 64-bit arithmetic and passes a check written as offset + length <= file length. The rule is offset <= file length and length <= file length - offset, which no pair can wrap

cases.name: v1-metadata-overlaps-header
cases.reason: an extent inside the file that covers the header's second half and the group table. A block shares no byte with the header, a table, a block index or a block

cases.name: v1-metadata-overlaps-a-block
cases.reason: an extent over the first data block's first 16 bytes. Read as a block it would be bytes the CRC covers for another purpose

cases.name: v1-metadata-misplaced
cases.reason: a well-formed block after the level tables, overlapping nothing. A block lies directly after the channel table and before the first data block, so a file has one layout for one content

cases.name: v1-metadata-block-over-bound
cases.reason: 1,048,577 bytes, one more than the block bound, made by lengthening one description of the at-bound conformance file by one byte. That description is now 1,025 bytes, over its own bound too, and the block bound is checked first, so the class is the block's

cases.name: v1-metadata-invalid-utf8-byte
cases.reason: one byte 0xFF inside a description. No UTF-8 sequence contains it

cases.name: v1-metadata-encoded-surrogate
cases.reason: ED A0 80, the three-byte encoding of the surrogate U+D800. Strict UTF-8 does not encode surrogates, so the span is not UTF-8; a decoder that passes surrogates through is not a strict one

cases.name: v1-metadata-whitespace
cases.reason: one space after a colon. The form has no insignificant whitespace

cases.name: v1-metadata-leading-bom
cases.reason: a byte-order mark before the object. It is valid UTF-8 and it is not part of the form

cases.name: v1-metadata-members-unsorted
cases.reason: provenance before channels. Members are in ascending order of their names' UTF-8 bytes

cases.name: v1-metadata-duplicate-member
cases.reason: sig_a twice. A parser that keeps the last of two members serves "two"; one that keeps the first serves "one"; the form refuses both, because each name follows its predecessor strictly

cases.name: v1-metadata-escaped-duplicate
cases.reason: sig_a, then sig_a again spelled with a \u escape. Compared before unescaping the two differ; the form has no \u escape, so the block is refused without comparing them at all

cases.name: v1-metadata-unicode-escape
cases.reason: an e-acute written as \u00e9. The form writes every character raw except the quote and the backslash

cases.name: v1-metadata-lone-surrogate-escape
cases.reason: \ud800, a surrogate escape with no pair. The bytes are valid UTF-8, so this is not the UTF-8 class; the form has no \u escape, so it is this one

cases.name: v1-metadata-newline-escape
cases.reason: \n inside a description. A line break is a control character, which no string in a block holds, so the form needs no escape for it

cases.name: v1-metadata-raw-tab
cases.reason: a raw U+0009 inside a string, which no JSON string may hold

cases.name: v1-metadata-number
cases.reason: a number as a member's value. The form holds strings, objects and arrays and nothing else: no number, no null, no boolean

cases.name: v1-metadata-null
cases.reason: null where a description belongs. An unknown fact is an absent member, never a placeholder

cases.name: v1-metadata-trailing-bytes
cases.reason: a second value after the block's object

cases.name: v1-metadata-top-level-array
cases.reason: an array where the block's object belongs

cases.name: v1-metadata-provenance-missing
cases.reason: no provenance. A block says who wrote it and from what, or it is not written

cases.name: v1-metadata-sources-empty
cases.reason: an empty sources array. A writer stamps nothing without a named, hashed source, so a writer with none writes no block

cases.name: v1-metadata-writer-version-missing
cases.reason: writer_version absent; it is required beside writer

cases.name: v1-metadata-description-empty
cases.reason: an empty description. No string is empty: a channel with nothing to say has no key

cases.name: v1-metadata-description-not-a-string
cases.reason: an array where a description belongs. A description is a string

cases.name: v1-metadata-unknown-member
cases.reason: a member this reader does not know, with no may-ignore bit set that it does not implement. The block grows only behind a new bit, so an unknown member is refused at every depth; under such a bit it is skipped (v1_metadata_unknown_member_under_unknown_bit.tslod)

cases.name: v1-metadata-unknown-source-member
cases.reason: an unknown member inside a source: the rule holds at every depth

cases.name: v1-metadata-bidi-override
cases.reason: U+202E, a right-to-left override, inside a description. It makes text display as other text, so no string in a block carries a bidirectional override or isolate

cases.name: v1-metadata-c1-control
cases.reason: U+009B, a C1 control (the single-byte control sequence introducer), inside product. The form writes it raw, so it is canonical and refused here, with the other forbidden code points

cases.name: v1-metadata-noncharacter
cases.reason: U+FFFE, a noncharacter, inside a description. Valid UTF-8, and refused, as I-JSON refuses it

cases.name: v1-metadata-key-names-no-channel
cases.reason: sig_d, a name no channel in the file carries

cases.name: v1-metadata-key-is-a-prefix
cases.reason: sig, a prefix of three channel names and the name of none. Keys compare with names as whole strings

cases.name: v1-metadata-sha256-uppercase
cases.reason: the hash in uppercase hex. It is 64 lowercase hex digits, one spelling, so two writers stamp one source alike

cases.name: v1-metadata-sha256-short
cases.reason: 63 hex digits, one short of a SHA-256

cases.name: v1-metadata-source-name-is-a-path
cases.reason: a source named by a relative path. A name is a bare file name, so a file carries no directory of the machine that wrote it

cases.name: v1-metadata-source-name-backslash
cases.reason: the same path with a backslash separator

cases.name: v1-metadata-description-over-bound
cases.reason: a description of 513 code points and 1,026 UTF-8 bytes. The bound is 1,024 bytes of the decoded value, so a reader that counts code points accepts it and is wrong

cases.name: v1-metadata-provenance-string-over-bound
cases.reason: a firmware string of 257 bytes; every provenance string is at most 256

cases.name: v1-metadata-order-key-before-bound
cases.reason: two defects: sig_a's description is over its bound, and zz_none, which sorts after it, names no channel. The keys are judged before the bounds, so the class is the key's. A reader that walks the members once, judging each fully, meets sig_a first and gives the other class

cases.name: v1-metadata-order-grammar-before-provenance
cases.reason: two defects: an uppercase hash and an unknown provenance member. The grammar is judged before provenance's forms

cases.name: v1-metadata-order-file-defect-first
cases.reason: the block's pointer is past the end of the file, and sig_c's dtype is 10, outside the registry. The block is judged at the END of step 1, after every channel, level and block index entry, so the file is refused for the dtype and no block class is reported

cases.name: v1-metadata-file-read-on-past-a-refused-block
cases.reason: the block is refused, and channel sig_a's first data block's stored CRC has one bit flipped. A refused block does not end the read: the reader goes on to step 2 and refuses the file for the CRC, which is what reading on means

cases.name: v1-metadata-may-ignore-case-under-bit-32
cases.reason: the patch of v1-unknown-may-ignore-feature-bit-is-ACCEPTED in v1-negative-vectors: bit 32 set, bit 0 kept, the pointer bytes zero. A reader that does not implement bit 32 skips it, as that case says. One that does finds an empty extent at offset 0, refuses the block and opens the file — so that case's outcome holds for both
